The published theorem proves that the procedure returns D(grad f)(x)v for a finite C2 graph. Extracting its state and parameter blocks yields Hx and, using the Hessian-symmetry corollary, B^T x.
The published corollary states and proves symmetry of the Hessian of a C2 scalar field; this identifies the transposed mixed block from the HVP output.
The published theorem's actual Statement and complete proof give a unique local C1 branch for a C1 residual with zero and invertible state-block derivative, plus the derivative formula used here.

The published pointwise chain rule differentiates the residual-chart path gamma(t)=Psi(tr); its complete proof and zero-dimensional boundary handling were inspected.

The published mean-value inequality applies to the C1 path on each convex open subinterval epsilon/2<t<1-epsilon/2, where the derivative bound is uniform; continuity at the chart endpoints gives the state-residual estimate.
The published theorem's full contraction, invariant convex neighborhood, derivative-Lipschitz, C1 initialization, finite-K, and residual hypotheses are restated; its complete proof was inspected.
